title: Recursive characterization of canonical integral realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. On the small pro-etale sites of finite-type $k$-schemes use the strict semilinear system categories $\mathscr S_W$, reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W$, and actual adjunction unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use the operations $P_v,S_p,J_j,\otimes^L$ and their integral counterparts from [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], with $v$ separated finite type, $p$ proper and $j$ quasi-compact open. Restrict all input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Let $d_A$ be exactly the single-operation identification of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], including its specified localized open comparison. On these domains $u_K$ and $e_M$ are invertible. The canonical realization comparisons $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] are characterized by the following identities. For a variable, $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$. For a unary basic operation set
$$a_A(M)=d_A(\mathcal L M)\circ(\mathcal L A(e_M))^{-1}:\mathcal L A(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(\mathcal L M).$$
For tensor set
$$a_\otimes(M,N)=d_\otimes(\mathcal L M,\mathcal L N)\circ\bigl(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^L e_N)\bigr)^{-1}:\mathcal L(M\otimes^L N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L M\widehat\otimes^L\mathcal L N.$$
For $M=V(\mathcal R K_i)$ and $N=T(\mathcal R K_i)$, with independent leaf slots, the identities are
$$c_{AV}=A_{\rm int}(c_V)\circ a_A(M),\qquad c_{V\otimes T}=(c_V\widehat\otimes^Lc_T)\circ a_\otimes(M,N).$$
All these identities are natural in the input morphisms. This characterizes the specified comparisons themselves, including their normalization at a variable; it asserts no compatibility with shifts.

proof.text: The finite base field has characteristic p by its cardinality; the algebraic closure has the same characteristic. Since l and p are distinct primes, l is a unit in k. Map this unit along the structure map to the global sections of each scheme over k. Apply purNormalizedReconstruction, the counit clause of [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus], to the actual calculus of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Good systems are normalized, so their actual counits are invertible. This uses the existing reconstruction statement rather than repeating its effectivity argument.

proof.text: At a single variable, inputNormalization of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] says that the actual unit followed by the component of the comparison is the identity. That component is invertible, so the actual unit is invertible. The right triangle identity of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] likewise makes the unit at L M invertible whenever the counit at M is invertible, and identifies its inverse with L(e_M).

proof.text: For proper image, expand properA and properD, replace inverseOrZero by the genuine inverses established above, and apply naturality of realizationModel.push at e_M. The right triangle cancels the extra unit, giving precisely the proper comparison component. For an open immersion use openNormalization from [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. The unit at the target of openRealization is invertible by naturality along that isomorphism from the unit at L(J M). Cancel the mapped counit and target unit to identify openA with the specified openRealization component. For pullback the defining d is the isomorphism of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. For tensor, the tensor of the two invertible counits and its image under L are invertible. These arguments give every field of OperationLaws.

proof.text: Induct on BasicTree. For variables inputNormalization and inverse uniqueness identify the component with the inverse actual unit. For pullback cancel the invertible L P(e_M) in the recorded pull equation of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. For proper image and open extension substitute the identifications of the preceding step into its push and shriek equations. For tensor cancel L(e_M tensor e_N) in its tensor equation. Admissibility supplies Good for each child, and the induction hypotheses supply all the nested Equations clauses. Compact-support vertices are excluded by BasicTree.

proof.text: For uniqueness induct on the same tree. At a variable, both components equal the inverse actual unit. At each unary vertex, rewrite both components by their recursion equations and apply the child equality evaluated on the restricted input object. At a tensor vertex apply the two child equalities separately, so independent input slots are retained. Componentwise equality gives equality of natural transformations and then of natural isomorphisms. Naturality is already part of these natural isomorphisms; no detection of equality by finite evaluation is used.

Step 2: the right triangle identity gives u_{LM}=L(e_M)^{-1}; RK is normalized; naturality along the existence-only h: LRK->K makes u_K invertible. I checked by hand: r_A = e R(d_A^{-1}) from the generator statement; the R-L transpose b=L(q)u and its inverse q=e_M R(b); the single-operation transpose d_A^{-1}; the unary formula b_{AV}=LA(e_M)d_A(LM)^{-1}A_int(b_V) and its inverse A_int(c_V)a_A(M); the tensor case with two-input d_tensor naturality; and the counit-naturality equations for the inverse LA(e) factors. Hypotheses at intermediate stages hold because I_V is isomorphic to LM (complete, constructible) and R I_V to M (normalized). Small cases: leaf gives u^{-1}; one operation gives d_A; zero input and empty open give zero maps; R[0] at a point. The coefficient categories are the same as in the parent. One formal point, which I accept: the parent's statement does not fix the leaf normalization, so the identification with the parent's c_V in step 6 uses the parent's step-4 definitions.
